verdicts.reason: Y's witness-value flip directly blocks rigged unconditional-FAIL checks, and its 10-brief test with kill thresholds and an ambition guard is far more decisive than X's single-brief test.

Y re-extracts claims and re-runs a frozen check so revisions cannot game the check, penalises struck load-bearing claims, and tests against a matched-token prose-feedback control on 10 briefs with kill criteria.

Y adds codebase probes so the checkable-claim assumption holds for this qualitative brief, measures the checkable fraction in a step 0 with a kill rule, and gives low-check cards the pool median instead of last place.

Y is standalone, restricted to finalists with a hard token cap, reverts cards that fall under 3 claims, and can be tested offline on saved benchmark cards, whereas X depends on a ledger that may not exist and costs roughly 2x development tokens.
